pages.title: Why NBT Matters
pages.text: Most blocks and items only need their $(bold)type$() and $(bold)count$() in a blueprint (e.g., "64× Stone"). But some items are $(bold)functionally different$() even when they share the same item ID — their NBT data determines what they actually do.$(br2)$(bold)Example: PreFab Blocks$()$(br2)A PreFab producing 100 diamonds/tick and a PreFab producing 1 dirt/tick are both `fpscompress:prefab_machine` items. Without NBT tracking, a blueprint would accept either one interchangeably — but their cached production rates are completely different.$(br2)NBT-aware scanning ensures blueprints only accept items with matching NBT for the fields that matter.

pages.title: How It Works
pages.text: $(li)$(bold)JSON schemas$() define which blocks/items have important NBT fields (see Data Pack Configuration below) $(li)$(bold)During scanning$(), the Fabricator checks each block/item against the NBT registry $(li)If a match is found, the specified NBT fields are extracted and stored in the blueprint $(li)$(bold)During printing$(), the Fabricator validates that provided resources match both the item ID $(bold)and$() the required NBT fields $(li)Items with wrong or missing NBT are automatically $(bold)rejected$() (returned to player inventory or dropped)

pages.title: What Gets Tracked
pages.text: By default, FPSCompress ships with one NBT requirement:$(br2)$(li)$(bold)`fpscompress:prefab_machine`:$() `importerExporterRates` (list subset, ignoring UUIDs) - Ensures printed PreFabs have matching cached production rates$(br2)You can add more via datapacks (see below).$(br2)---
